newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston agrees to sell Ganis unit.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston agrees to sell Ganis unit.

text.p: BankBoston Corp said Tuesday it had agreed to sell its Ganis Credit Corp unit to Deutsche Financial Services, part of the Deutsche Bank AG group, for $30 million.
BankBoston said Deutsche Financial, based in St. Louis, will acquire the personnel, systems and origination capabilities of Ganis, a consumer credit business.
A large portion of Ganis's loan portfolio, about $1.0 billion in recreational vehicle and marine boat loans, has been sold separately from the transaction with Deutsche Financial, BankBoston said.

Ganis, based in Newport Beach, Calif., is a nationwide business with annual loan originations of $700 million. All 160 employees, operating from 12 offices across the U.S., will be offered positions with Deutsche Financial, BankBoston said.

"While Ganis has been a successful franchise for us, we believe that our capital would be better directed toward investments that support our existing key businesses, where we can leverage our dollars and cross-sell our products and services," BankBoston Chief Executive Charles Gifford said in a statement.

John Fraher, deputy director of investor relations, said in answer to a query that the transaction would be a breakeven on the income statement because BankBoston paid about $30 million for the unit in 1995.

Regarding the sale of the loan portfolio, he said some will be recorded on the company's books in the first quarter and some in the second quarter. He said the company expects a minor gain of less than $10 million.
He said the transaction will take about $1.0 billion of loans off the balance sheet and free up about $70 million in capital.
